packet.evidence_limit: Review covers the submitted passage and its editing rationale. Several voices and arrangements can serve the same reader. Whether real readers understood it needs a reader observation. Fiction, poetry, the learner's overall talent and any private writing remain outside this finding.
packet.goal: I want to learn how to be a better writer
packet.learner: Can we try two versions of the lamp notice, one with the line about volunteers and one without? I want to see which is easier to scan.

material.practice: A fictional choir's note says, 'Return folders to their places.' Borrowed folders go to the conductor. Singers keep their own folders. Revise the note, then identify the edit that helps a new singer decide what to do.
material.worked: A garden note says, 'Put it in the right pile.' The brief sends dry leaves to the compost heap and fallen branches to the shed. 'Compost the dry leaves. Stack fallen branches at the shed.' The concrete nouns tell a gardener which line applies. A single flowing sentence could carry the same distinction.

packet.new_task: Write a short onboarding note for a new library volunteer shelving returns. Items with a blue dot stay on the cart for staff to check. Unmarked items go on the shelves. The draft says, 'Put the returns where they belong.' Revise it in your own voice and explain one edit that helps the new volunteer decide what to do.
packet.policy: Ask for a passage from the new task. If an approved goal is available, show it and ask whether it fits this task. If it fits, use it with the new passage to choose a worked example and a practice prompt that targets a specific choice in the draft. Otherwise, ask what the writer wants the passage to do for its reader and teach from that answer. After practice, ask the writer to explain in their own words how their choice serves the current purpose. Update the saved goal only with explicit approval of the new wording.

receipt.goal: I want to learn how to be a better writer

response.display: Paste your lamp notice, including the line about volunteers, so we can compare it with a version that leaves that line out. Your saved goal is “I want to learn how to be a better writer.” Does that fit what you want to practice here? As we compare the versions, we can use the garden note as a model and look at which words help a reader quickly spot what to do.
